hypothesis: The device clock (37.5 MHz on the U280) is held down by a few structural paths, not by the design's depth in general; cutting them without changing any cycle count raises the clock the board can build at, and generating the FMA with XLS instead of hand-placing its stages makes the next step (a deeper FMA) a configuration change.
evidence_for_hypothesis: U280 link, clk_dev worst path: tnca_matrix g_mac[12] p1_mag_reg -> p0_exp_common_reg, 60 logic levels, 23.931 ns routed (73% route), slack 2.689 ns at 26.668 ns -- the FMA's normalise/round, the accumulator file's write-to-read bypass, and the next multiply-add's operand multiply and alignment in one cycle (doc/r38_board_bringup.md sec 6.1)

microarch.change: accumulator file read-old (no write-to-read bypass; tnca_matrix checks in simulation that nothing reads a row in the cycle it is written); the binary32 FMA generated by XLS from xls/tnca_fma.x (no apfloat: subnormals kept), instance chosen by LAT = FP_LAT (2: the old shape; 3: one stage deeper); the tensor engine's box element count computed while the TensorMap loads (one multiply per word) so S_TCHK compares instead of multiplying five times; device clock divider a parameter, DEV_DIV = 3 (50 MHz) for new builds. Generation and measurement: two FMA entries in the XLS config (per-module clock period and flop_outputs); out-of-context post-synthesis timing of a unit or the device in minutes (make fpga-timing)

compatibility.cycles: unchanged: FP_LAT stays 2 and the generated latency-2 FMA has the hand-written module's register count and position of the result (combinational from the last stage); the bypass removed never carried a used value; the box check moved to cycles that were already spent waiting for the TensorMap
compatibility.artifacts: unchanged: no compiler, target or ISA change
compatibility.numerics: unchanged: the generated FMA at both latencies matches the exact Fraction oracle on 41 240 (unit) and 516 240 (fma-deep) vectors, and tb_fpu_multi on 5 012 across the five formats
compatibility.board: the image loaded on 2026-10-08 (uuid 083faace...) is DEV_DIV = 4 (37.5 MHz) and stays valid; BOARD_CLOCK_HZ changes with the image that is loaded

resource.kind: Vivado 2023.2 post-synthesis, out of context, xcu280-fsvh2892-2L-e, 13.333 ns target (flow/synth/vivado_ooc.sh)

parent.worst_path: u_txf t_b0 -> st (tensor window check); the matrix accumulate loop measured 14.735 ns / 67 levels in tnca_matrix alone

change.worst_path: VRF bank BRAM read -> tnca_matrix A element -> widen -> FMA stage 0

tnca_tensor.after: no longer among the device's worst paths

resource.note: post-synthesis estimates; the one path measured both ways (the matrix loop) ran 1.6x longer routed (23.931 ns) than estimated (14.735 ns). The device's parent figure (10.099 ns) is with the bypass already removed; before that its worst was the 60-level loop.

results.clock: new builds divide the 150 MHz kernel clock by 3: 50 MHz, 20.0 ns, against an estimated 16.3 ns routed worst path. Not yet linked; link.sh fails rather than lowers the clock.
results.next: 75 MHz (13.3 ns) needs about 8.3 ns post-synthesis: register the matrix A operand before the FMA or select FP_LAT = 3 (the latency-3 instance exists); either changes cycles, so it is a separate design change with a re-frozen baseline
results.correctness: unit (both FMA latencies), fma-deep (both), lint (50 files), core 31/31 and core-vrf 31/31 (including the tensor descriptor programs t12, t17, t33-t35), r38-xpose-rtl, top, e2e; cycle counts as before (t10_mesh 18 591)

rollback: DEV_DIV = 4 restores the old clock; the FMA instance and the box precomputation are behaviour-identical to what they replace
